title: Who Is the Man
hook: Valmiki asked a question too large for an ordinary afternoon.
body: The sage wanted one name: a man complete in courage, conduct, and truth, pleasing to look at and harder to shake. Narada, who walks between heaven and earth, had come to the hermitage as if the question had called him.
line: Valmiki did not want a god described from a distance. He wanted a life that could be told, with a kingdom, a wife, a war, and a cost.

title: Narada Sits
hook: The visitor set down his vina and answered without hedging.
body: There is such a man, Narada said. His name is Rama. He is the son of Dasharatha of Ayodhya, and the virtues you listed are not scattered in him. They sit in one body.
line: He is gentle with the weak and finished with the cruel. People trust him before they can explain why. That, Narada said, is the man.

title: The List
hook: Narada did not praise in a cloud. He counted.
body: Rama knows the Vedas and the bow. He keeps his word when the word turns expensive. He does not take another man's wife, and he does not abandon one who comes to him.
line: Anger in him has a gate. Mercy in him has a spine. Narada spoke as a man who had already seen the end of the story and still found the beginning worth telling.

title: The Story in Brief
hook: Then Narada told the whole epic in one sitting, and left.
body: Exile. A deer of gold. A wife taken through the sky. An alliance with the vanaras. A bridge. A war. A return. He gave Valmiki the bones of the poem so the poet would know he was not inventing a rumor.
line: When Narada rose, the hermitage felt larger and less peaceful. A question had been answered. A labor had begun.

title: The Tamasa
hook: Valmiki went to the river with a disciple, meaning only to bathe.
body: The water was clear enough to show the stones. The poet was pleased, in the small way a person is pleased by a clean place. He had not come looking for a meter.
line: The bank was ordinary. That is what the epic trusts you to notice later: the first verse did not arrive in a court.

title: The Pair
hook: Two krauncha birds were playing in the shallows, a life with no audience.
body: They moved as one habit. The poet watched them the way a person watches something that does not need him. For a moment the Ramayana was not in his head at all.
line: Joy, in this book, is often shown just before it is struck.

title: The Hunter
hook: A nishada shot the male. The female cried, and did not stop.
body: The arrow was skillful. That was the obscenity of it. Valmiki saw the bird fall and heard a grief that had no manners and no plan.
line: The poet, who had asked about perfect conduct, was suddenly angry at a perfect shot.

title: The First Shloka
hook: Grief left his mouth already measured.
body: Ma nishada. The words came in four even feet, a curse that was also a verse. He had not chosen the form. The form had arrived inside the pain.
line: His disciple repeated it, astonished. The meter of the Ramayana was born as a refusal to let a cruel skill stand unnamed.

title: Brahma Comes
hook: The creator stood in the hermitage and told him what the verse was for.
body: You will write Rama's whole life, Brahma said, what Narada told you and what no one told you. Nothing true will hide from you while you compose.
line: The curse on a hunter had been a doorway. The poem would have to walk through fourteen years, a war, and a sorrow even the hero would not be spared.

title: He Writes
hook: Valmiki sat down and the knowing came as work, not as magic that skipped the work.
body: Day after day the leaf filled. Sita's voice. Lakshmana's watch. The bridge. The fire. He wrote what he had not seen, and it did not feel like invention. It felt like memory that had been waiting for a hand.
line: A poem this long is a kind of vow. He kept it.

title: Two Students
hook: He did not keep the poem in a chest. He put it in two boys.
body: Lava and Kusha learned every chapter until the epic could stand up without the poet in the room. Their voices were young. The sorrow they carried was not.
line: Valmiki taught them to sing it whole, including the pages that would hurt the man who heard them.

title: They Know It Whole
hook: A song is not learned when it is pretty. It is learned when it can be repeated on a tired day.
body: The twins walked the hermitage singing exile, the deer, the sea, the war. Birds got used to the sound. The poem became a path their feet knew.
line: Valmiki listened for the places they softened, and sent them back. Mercy in the telling still had to be exact.

title: In Rama's Hearing
hook: They sang it in Ayodhya, in the court of the king the poem was about.
body: Rama did not know their names as his sons. He knew the story as his life. The hall went still in the way a hall does when it realizes the song is not entertainment.
line: The boys did not flinch at the hard pages. They had been taught that accuracy is a form of respect.

title: He Knows the Song
hook: Rama heard his own grief given back to him in a child's mouth.
body: The frame of the epic closes on its subject. The king who will live these chapters is already, in the poem's first book, listening to them.
line: Valmiki's question had found its man. The man now had to sit still and be told.

title: Ayodhya
hook: Before the sons, the poem builds the city that will miss them.
body: Wide roads, full granaries, towers like a range of white hills. The people were not decorations. They were the reason a king's private vow could become a public wound.
line: Valmiki lingers here. A paradise in a poem is only useful if you later understand what it costs to leave it.

title: The Gates
hook: Traders, horses, and priests moved through the same morning.
body: No one in the street was rehearsing a tragedy. That is the city's innocence, and the poem does not mock it. Happiness can be intelligent and still not see the day it ends.
line: Ayodhya's strength was order. Order is what Dasharatha trusted more than his own heart.

title: Dasharatha
hook: He had fought well and ruled long, and the one room in him was empty.
body: Three queens: Kausalya, Kaikeyi, Sumitra. A court that worked. A line that stopped at his own life. Age had begun to feel like a question he could not hand to a minister.
line: A king without a son is not only a father without a child. He is a city without a next morning.

title: The Council
hook: Sumantra spoke for the house. Vashishtha kept the rites from becoming theater.
body: Eight ministers held the practical kingdom: roads, grain, justice, the dull holiness of things that must be counted. Dasharatha listened. He was not a fool king. He was a complete king with one missing piece.
line: The poem will need you to remember that. The disaster later is not born from incompetence.

title: The Empty Side
hook: He said it aloud at last, because silence had become heavier than speech.
body: I have no son to take this throne. The words were simple. The hall treated them as a structural fact, like a crack in a wall everyone had agreed not to touch.
line: Kausalya heard them as a wife. The city heard them as a future.

title: A King's Remedy
hook: The priests named the old cure: a horse sacrifice, the ashvamedha, and the rite that asks for a son.
body: Dasharatha agreed the way a drowning man agrees to a rope. It would cost a year, a fortune, and the attention of every holy man he could gather.
line: He did not yet know that the rope had a name, and that the name lived in a forest, wearing a horn.

title: Sumantra Remembers
hook: The minister had been carrying an old prophecy the way a careful man carries a sealed letter.
body: Sanatkumara had said Dasharatha's sons would be born through Rishyashringa, the deer-horned sage, and through the rite that sage would perform. Sumantra spoke it now, because the moment had opened.
line: A kingdom's future, it turned out, depended on a boy who had never seen a city.

title: Anga Without Rain
hook: Before Ayodhya's rite, the poem tells why Rishyashringa already belonged to a king.
body: Romapada ruled Anga, and Anga had gone dry. The clouds passed over as if the land had been struck from their list. Crops failed. The priests traced the drought to a slighted offering, a brahmin unanswered.
line: A kingdom can be punished in weather. Romapada learned that in his fields.

title: Romapada's Fear
hook: He was not a villain. He was a man who had delayed a duty until the sky noticed.
body: The court offered politics. The brahmins offered a name. Only Rishyashringa, raised outside the sight of women, could stand in the rite that would persuade the rain.
line: Romapada, who had once received Dasharatha's daughter Shanta as his own, now had to fetch a sage who did not know what a court was.

title: The Only Name
hook: Bring him gently, the counselors said. Force will fail on a boy who has never been commanded by desire.
body: They did not mean armies. They meant women who understood welcome, sweets he had no word for, a beauty that would look, to him, like a new kind of forest.
line: The plan was a trick. The poem does not pretend otherwise. It also shows the rain that followed.

title: Vibhandaka
hook: The father had built a world with one rule: nothing in it would teach his son longing.
body: Rishyashringa was born of the sage's austerity, marked with a horn, raised among deer and hymns. Women were not a subject. They were an absence his education depended on.
line: Vibhandaka believed purity was a closed gate. The epic is about to test the gate.

title: The Horned Boy
hook: He was not a monster in the telling. He was a child who had been given only half a world.
body: He fetched water. He tended the fire. He could hear a deer before he saw it. When his father left to gather roots, the hut became the whole map.
line: Innocence this complete is not stupid. It is unprotected.

title: Among Deer
hook: The animals were his brothers, because no one else had been offered.
body: He did not experience this as poverty. The forest fed him, the hymns named the day, and his father's return was the evening. A life can be full and still be one breath away from breaking.
line: Far off, a dry kingdom was already walking toward that breath.

title: The Sending
hook: Romapada chose courtesans, not soldiers, which is its own kind of intelligence and its own kind of shame.
body: They were told to look like the forest's own kindness. No seizure. No sermon. A visit that would feel, to the boy, like hospitality from heaven.
line: Shanta waited in the city, not knowing she was about to marry a man who had never heard of marriage.

title: A False Ashram
hook: They made a bright place near his hut, flowers and food and laughter kept low.
body: It was a stage. It was also, for a few days, the first beautiful thing in his life that his father had not authorized. The poem lets both sentences stand.
line: When he came looking for roots, the roots had company.

title: He Sees Them
hook: He asked what they were, because his categories had run out.
body: They said they were a kind of sage, which was a lie shaped like a courtesy. They did not seize him. They let him look. Looking, for him, was already a journey.
line: The horned boy had been trained to distrust nothing that smiled. The training worked exactly as far as the city needed.

title: The Sweets
hook: They fed him things his father had never named.
body: Cakes, fruit cooked in sugar, a welcome that entered by the mouth because the mind had no defense prepared there. He thought this must be how great sages lived when his father was away.
line: Pleasure, met for the first time, feels like revelation. That is why it is dangerous, and why it is also a kind of truth.

title: He Follows
hook: They asked him to their place. He went, because refusal was a skill he had never practiced on kindness.
body: The path out of the forest was short. The path out of his education was the rest of his life. He did not look back at the hut until the trees had already changed.
line: Behind him, a father was about to come home to an answer he had spent a childhood preventing.

title: The Empty Hut
hook: Vibhandaka returned and found the fire cold and the boy gone.
body: Rage in a sage is a weather of its own. He understood at once that the world had done what the world does: it had walked in through the door he had called virtue.
line: He went after his son. Love and fury, in him, were not opposites.

title: The Rain
hook: When Rishyashringa's foot entered Anga, the sky remembered the fields.
body: Water came down on roofs that had learned the sound of dust. Romapada went out into it like a man forgiven. The trick and the miracle occupied the same hour, which is why the story has lasted.
line: A boy's first disobedience watered a kingdom.

title: Shanta
hook: Romapada gave him Shanta, the daughter he had raised, and the marriage made the rite legal in the human way.
body: In the older telling Shanta is Dasharatha's child, given to his friend. The knot between the two kings was already tied in a girl before it was tied in a sacrifice.
line: Rishyashringa, who had not known what a wife was, learned a household. His father, arriving in anger, saw the rain and the girl and at last allowed the life to stand.

title: Dasharatha Asks
hook: Ayodhya's king sent love, gifts, and a need he could no longer decorate.
body: Come, he told Romapada. Lend me the sage who brought you rain. My city is not dry of water. It is dry of a future. Rishyashringa must light the rite.
line: Romapada, who owed his sky to that boy, did not pretend the debt was small.

title: The Road to Ayodhya
hook: Rishyashringa entered a city that was the opposite of his childhood.
body: Drums, elephants, women in the windows, a king who came out of the gate rather than waiting to be approached. Shanta came with him. The horned sage looked at the towers as a forest looks at a second forest.
line: Dasharatha bowed to the boy who would give him sons. Rank, for an hour, ran backward, and it was correct.

title: He Is Honored
hook: They gave him a house worthy of the work, and did not treat him as a tool they had rented.
body: Vashishtha received him as a colleague in the sacred, not as a curiosity. The court learned to look at the horn without whispering. Awe, if it is any good, becomes manners.
line: The sacrifice could begin, because the man who had to sit at its center had been given a seat.

title: The Horse Is Loosed
hook: A consecrated horse walked out of Ayodhya, and the kingdom's claim walked with it.
body: For a year the animal would wander. Where it went, Dasharatha's arms had to be ready to say: this ground is under our protection, or this ground accepts the rite. It was politics braided into worship.
line: Rama was not born yet. Already the world was being asked to make room.

title: A Year of Guarding
hook: The king's men followed the horse the way a sentence follows its subject.
body: There were challenges, because a wandering claim is a provocation. Dasharatha held them without turning the rite into a conquest. The poem is brief here. It wants the year to pass so the fire can begin.
line: When the horse came home, the city smelled of the next chapter.

title: The Altar
hook: They built the ground as carefully as other men build forts.
body: Brick, mantra, the queens in their places, Rishyashringa at the heart of the recitation. Dasharatha gave away so much wealth that the priests had to tell him to stop performing generosity and let the rite finish.
line: A son cannot be purchased. The king was not purchasing. He was making himself empty enough to receive.

title: Putrakameshti
hook: Beside the horse sacrifice they set the rite whose only request was children.
body: Rishyashringa chanted with the steadiness of someone who had grown up talking to fire. The queens fasted and watched. A city can hold its breath. Ayodhya did.
line: Into that attention, the flame thickened.

title: Out of the Fire
hook: A being rose, not quite a man, carrying a golden bowl.
body: This is payasam, he said, prepared by the gods. Give it to your queens. Then he was gone, as if the fire had only borrowed a body long enough to hand something over.
line: Dasharatha held the bowl the way a man holds a future that could still be spilled.

title: Divide This
hook: He did not drink it himself. The instruction was a distribution.
body: Half went to Kausalya. Of what remained, half to Sumitra, then a share to Kaikeyi, and the last of it to Sumitra again. The portions were unequal on purpose. Sumitra, given twice, would bear twice.
line: Three women, one sweetness, four lives waiting inside the arithmetic.

title: What Each Received
hook: Kausalya carried the largest share, and the eldest hope.
body: Kaikeyi's share was smaller and would become Bharata, which the later books will refuse to treat as smaller. Sumitra's two portions were a quiet prophecy: Lakshmana and Shatrughna, the brothers who would live as shadows and as shields.
line: The bowl was empty. The months were not.

title: The Months
hook: The queens grew heavy, and the city practiced joy before the proof.
body: Songs were composed in advance, which is a kind of faith. Dasharatha walked more softly in his own halls. A man who has wanted a thing for decades becomes careful when it finally agrees to arrive.
line: Winter turned. The ninth of Chaitra was coming up the calendar like a name.

title: The Night Before
hook: Ayodhya did not sleep well, and nobody minded.
body: Lamps were counted. Midwives waited. Kausalya, who had carried the largest hope the longest, entered the hour the way a queen enters a gate she cannot send a servant through.
line: Somewhere in the poem's frame, a poet was already writing this dawn. Inside the story, it had not happened yet.

title: Four Births
hook: On the ninth of the bright half of Chaitra, Rama was born to Kausalya.
body: Bharata followed to Kaikeyi. Sumitra bore Lakshmana and Shatrughna. The cries were ordinary and the meaning was not. Drums went through streets that had been rehearsing this sound for a year.
line: Dasharatha, old in the wanting, was young for a morning.

title: The Names
hook: Vashishtha spoke them, and the names stuck as if the boys had arrived already wearing them.
body: Rama. Bharata. Lakshmana. Shatrughna. Four words the rest of the epic will not be able to put down. Even the servants said them carefully, the way people say a thing they expect to be praying with later.
line: A dynasty is first of all a list of names that a city agrees to love.

title: The City
hook: Ayodhya did what a happy city does: it spent.
body: Grain, gold, elephants painted, poor households suddenly inside the festival rather than beside it. Dasharatha gave until the priests laughed and told him the boys were already born, he could stop bribing the universe.
line: For a few days the epic allows delight to be uncomplicated.

title: Already Paired
hook: Even in the nursery the brothers sorted themselves.
body: Lakshmana cried when Rama was carried to another room. Shatrughna settled only when Bharata was near. Nurses gossiped about it, and the gossip was accurate. The epic's great loyalties begin as infant weather.
line: Two pairs. One house. A pattern the war will not break.

title: Vashishtha's House
hook: The priest took the boys the way a river takes rain, as his work and his joy.
body: They learned hymns before they learned flattery. The staff, the bow, the way to sit when an elder entered. Rama listened as if the lesson were a person he did not want to interrupt.
line: Childhood in this book is not a blank. It is training.

title: The Bow as a Lesson
hook: They were princes, so the weapon was a language, not a toy.
body: Rama's hand settled on the string early. The masters noticed and did not rush him. A gift that is hurried becomes a performance. They wanted a competence that would still be there when the audience was gone.
line: Lakshmana learned by watching Rama learn, which would remain his method.

title: A Boy's Steadiness
hook: The stories of his childhood are small, and the poem treats smallness as evidence.
body: He did not mock a servant. He did not take the last sweet as a right. When he was hurt he did not make the hurt a government. People who look for spectacle miss the point. Character is what repeats.
line: Dasharatha watched and felt the dangerous tenderness of a father who knows his son is better than he is.

title: They Grow
hook: Years in Ayodhya can pass as a single golden weather.
body: The boys became youths. Their shoulders took the bows seriously. Kausalya's face changed in the mirror and she allowed it, because the reason was walking in the courtyard.
line: Bharata and Shatrughna would soon go to their grandfather's house in Kekaya. The poem plants that absence early, like a seed it intends to need.

title: The People Already Know
hook: A city decides who its next king is before the ceremony does.
body: Market talk, women's talk at the well, soldiers who had seen Rama in the yard: the verdict was the same. If the throne had asked the streets, the streets would not have needed a meeting.
line: Dasharatha heard it and was glad, and also afraid, because love that wide is a thing that can be broken in public.

title: A Knock at the Age of Peace
hook: The morning Vishwamitra came, nothing in Ayodhya was wrong.
body: That is the shape of this book. The crisis does not grow out of rot. It arrives at a gate, polite, matted, and impossible to refuse without becoming smaller than the guest.
line: The guards announced a sage. The king stood up. Childhood, without a speech, ended.

title: Vishwamitra Enters
hook: The sage did not come as a beggar. He came as a man the gods owed answers to.
body: Dasharatha rose, offered water, a seat, the whole grammar of honor. Vishwamitra accepted it without wasting it on small talk. He had walked out of a sacrifice that demons were spoiling, and he wanted a specific boy.
line: The court felt the temperature change, the way a room does when the real subject arrives.

title: The Welcome
hook: For a day the visit looked like any other holy arrival.
body: Food, praise, the story of the sage's long war with his own anger, which had ended in a power even the gods consulted. Rama watched from the side, a youth being shown what an ascetic who has finished becoming looks like.
line: Vishwamitra let himself be hosted. Hospitality was not the request. It was the pause before it.

title: He Names Rama
hook: Then he said the sentence the welcome had been holding.
body: Give me Rama. The demons Maricha and Subahu foul my sacrifice. Your armies will not do. I need the boy, and I need him for a handful of nights. I will return him to you.
line: The hall heard a sage ask for a prince the way a man asks for a tool that happens to be someone's child.

title: A Father's No
hook: Dasharatha answered as a father first, which is why the answer was insufficient.
body: He is not sixteen in the way a weapon is sixteen. He has not stood in a war. Take me. Take the army. Take the elephants. Do not take the morning I have only just been given.
line: The king was not wrong about the danger. He was wrong about who the boy was.

title: Take Me Instead
hook: He offered his own aging body as if love could be swapped unit for unit.
body: Vishwamitra did not insult the offer. He refused it. A king's courage was not the shape required. The shape required was Rama's, and the sage had not walked this far to negotiate a substitute.
line: Dasharatha sat down inside his no, and found it already cracking.

title: Vashishtha Speaks
hook: The royal priest told the king the truth that fathers hear as cruelty.
body: This guest is not a neighbor who has overasked. He is Vishwamitra. The boy is not only your son. If you refuse, you refuse dharma wearing a father's face, and the sage's anger will be a second drought.
line: Vashishtha did not say Rama would be safe. He said Rama was the one the errand had been shaped for.

title: The Consent
hook: Dasharatha gave the boy with both hands, which is the only honest way to give what you hate to give.
body: He called Rama and Lakshmana, because Lakshmana would not have stayed if the calling had forgotten him. The sage looked at the pair and nodded as if the second had been included in the first.
line: A father can obey and still be broken. The poem lets him be both.

title: They Leave at Dawn
hook: The city that had just learned their names watched them walk out behind a sage.
body: No chariot. The lesson had already started: princes who cannot walk will be useless in the forest they are going to meet. Kausalya did not make a scene. The scene was the leaving.
line: Dasharatha stood until the small figures were a grammar of distance.

title: Bala and Atibala
hook: On the first road Vishwamitra gave them two vidyas, Bala and Atibala.
body: Not weapons yet. A way of not tiring, of not going hungry, of keeping the mind clear when the body wanted to negotiate. Rama received them as he received everything from this teacher: completely, without display.
line: The forest began as a classroom that did not announce itself.

title: A Spoiled Wood
hook: The trees changed before the demon did. That is how a curse occupies land.
body: Vishwamitra told them they were entering Tataka's forest. Birds had left. The light arrived tired. A place can be guilty without being confused about who did it.
line: Rama listened to the history before he was asked to act on it. The sage did not want a boy who shot first and understood later.

title: Who She Was
hook: Tataka had been a yaksha's daughter, strong enough that strength became her weather.
body: Suketu begot her. She married Sunda. She bore Maricha. A curse and a grief turned her hunger into a reign over a forest people had abandoned. The poem gives her a before, so the killing is not of a fog.
line: Rama was being asked to end a person, not a rumor.

title: Her Son
hook: Maricha was already a name in the sage's grievance, and a name the later forest would reuse.
body: Vishwamitra did not pretend the family was simple. A mother, a son, a second demon Subahu: the sacrifice ahead was being interrupted by a house, not by a random storm.
line: Rama held that complication and did not use it as a reason to do nothing. Compassion that cannot act is only a mood.

title: They Cross In
hook: The air smelled of a place that had not been prayed in for a long time.
body: Lakshmana walked half a step behind, which was already his vow. Vishwamitra's staff made the only civilized sound. Rama's eyes had gone to the work. Youth left his face without announcement.
line: Somewhere in the spoiled green, something large turned toward the sound of three people who had not asked permission.

title: She Comes
hook: Tataka arrived as weather that had decided to wear a body.
body: Dust, a roar, the size of her. She was not a riddle. She was the reason the forest had no villages. Rama saw her and still did not loose, because the last instruction in his hands was a hesitation about killing a woman.
line: The sage had expected that hesitation. He had brought a teaching, not only a guard.

title: He Hesitates
hook: Vishwamitra answered the hesitation in the open, so the killing would not be private from conscience.
body: Cruelty wearing any form is still the thing a king is for. She is not a woman you are being asked to humiliate. She is a power that has emptied a country. If you will not end it, you are choosing the villages.
line: Rama heard it as dharma, not as permission to enjoy the shot.

title: The Arrow
hook: He shot, and the forest got its sound back.
body: Tataka fell. The poem does not dance on the body. It records a necessary end and the quiet afterward, which was birds returning in their minds before they returned in fact. Lakshmana looked at his brother and saw the boy and the king in the same hour.
line: Vishwamitra said nothing decorative. The next gift was already in the air.

title: The Gods Approve
hook: They had been watching, which in this book means they were about to arm him.
body: A voice, or the pressure of many voices, told Vishwamitra the prince was ready for what ordinary quivers do not hold. Rama stood in the cleared air and did not pose. Readiness in him looked like attention.
line: The sage lifted his hand. The sky answered with things that had names.

title: Named One by One
hook: The astras came as a catalog, and Rama had to receive each without swagger.
body: Fire, wind, the noose, the sleeper, the weapons of the directions. Vishwamitra spoke them. Rama repeated the mastery back, not as a boast but as a student proving the lesson had landed in the muscle.
line: Power arrived before comfort. It would keep arriving in that order.

title: He Accepts
hook: A weapon you cannot withdraw is not a gift. These could be called back.
body: That was the ethics hidden in the machinery. Rama learned the releasing and the unsaying. Lakshmana received his share and did not ask for Rama's. The hierarchy between them was love, not rivalry.
line: The forest, which had just lost Tataka, now held a boy who could unmake more than a demon if he was careless. He intended not to be.

title: Siddhashrama
hook: They reached the ashram where the sacrifice had been waiting like a held breath.
body: Vishwamitra said this ground had an older story: Vishnu, in another descent, had stood here and bound a king's pride. The present work was smaller and the same. Protect the fire until it finishes.
line: Rama and Lakshmana took the edges of the rite the way sentries take a wall.

title: Six Nights
hook: The demons did not come at once. Waiting was part of their weapon.
body: The brothers stood while priests chanted and the fire behaved. Youth discovers, in such hours, that glory is mostly not falling asleep at your post. Lakshmana took the later watches. Rama took the responsibility either way.
line: On the sixth night the sky tore.

title: Maricha and Subahu
hook: They came with blood in vessels, the old filth, poured toward the fire.
body: It was not a duel arranged for poets. It was an interruption meant to make the holy disgusting. Rama saw Maricha, Tataka's son, and did not confuse the son with the mother he had already ended.
line: Two targets. Two different sentences.

title: Flung Across the Sea
hook: Rama's arrow did not merely kill Maricha. It threw him.
body: The demon flew, a body becoming distance, and crashed into the ocean a hundred yojanas off, alive and finished with this forest. Subahu was not given that mercy. He fell here, and stayed fallen.
line: The fire did not go out. That was the victory the sage had walked to Ayodhya to buy.

title: The Fire Finishes
hook: Morning came to a sacrifice that had been allowed to complete.
body: Vishwamitra's face, which was not a face that performed gratitude, performed it anyway. He told the brothers to rest. They had done the errand. The king of Ayodhya would get his son back.
line: He did not say the road home would be a straight line. There was a city called Mithila, and a bow lying in it like a closed fate.

title: Toward Mithila
hook: They did not turn immediately back. The sage had more ground he wanted them to walk.
body: Janaka's city lay ahead, and between here and there the land was a library. Vishwamitra traveled by story as much as by road. Rama and Lakshmana learned that a journey with him would be longer on the inside than on the map.
line: The first tale waited at the next turn of the path.

title: He Begins a Tale
hook: Where other guides point at rivers, this one pointed at causes.
body: This countryside is not empty of events, he said. A god of desire walked here. A mountain caught a river. A woman waited as stone. If you only look at the trees you will think you are in a forest. You are in a memory.
line: Rama adjusted his pace to the pace of telling.

title: Kama Is Sent
hook: The gods, impatient with Shiva's austerity, sent desire to break it.
body: Kama went with a bow of sugarcane and arrows of flowers, which sounds gentle until you remember the target was the lord who had burned worlds by opening an eye. A mission can be made of blossoms and still be a suicide.
line: Rati, his wife, knew. She went anyway, because love does not always improve the odds.

title: The Sugarcane Bow
hook: He drew on Shiva while the great yogi sat like a shut door.
body: The arrow was spring. It touched the meditation the way scent touches a sleeper. For a moment even that stillness leaned toward Parvati, toward the world of pairs.
line: Then Shiva knew who had knocked, and the kindness of flowers was over.

title: The Eye Opens
hook: A point of fire on the brow, and Kama was ash.
body: No battle. A glance that was a furnace. The god of desire ended as a smear of gray on the air, and the gods who had sent him learned again that Shiva is not an instrument.
line: Rati's cry is the part the poem does not skip. A victory over desire still leaves a widow.

title: Ananga
hook: After that, desire had no body, which did not mean desire had no power.
body: He became Ananga, the bodiless one, which is a worse haunting than a man you can see. Shiva returned to stillness. The mountain kept a memory of heat.
line: Rama, hearing this with a bow on his own shoulder, understood that weapons are not the only things that undo a person.

title: Uma's Vow
hook: Parvati did not accept the refusal of the universe as her answer.
body: She set down the ornaments and took up tapas that made the mountain look lazy. If Shiva would not turn for a flower, he would have to turn for a will that outlasted flowers.
line: The poem gives her this page so the marriage of the great yogi is not something the gods arranged around her.

title: The Reed-Bed
hook: From the fire of that union, too fierce for one womb, a child was carried to a bed of reeds.
body: The kritikas nursed him. He became Kartikeya, the war-god with a spear, born because even ascetic fire eventually faces the world. Vishwamitra told it cleanly, without lingering on what was not the boys' to gawk at.
line: A spear in a thicket of reeds: that was the image he left in their hands, and walked on.

title: Why a River Was Needed
hook: Another story started with a horse, because royal vows often do.
body: Sagara, an ancestor in the solar line, set an ashvamedha. The horse was the claim. The sons were the army of the claim. When the horse vanished, a family mistake became a geological one.
line: Rama was walking beside the very river this mistake would one day require.

title: Sagara's Horse
hook: Two queens, two kinds of offspring: Asamanja the difficult one son, and from Sumati sixty thousand.
body: The number is the point. A king who asks the world for too much descent gets a crowd instead of a house. They were brave and they were many, which is not the same as being wise.
line: The horse went out. The sons followed. The earth, soon, would have to answer them.

title: The Horse Vanishes
hook: It was taken into the earth, and suspicion went with the searchers.
body: Indra had hidden it beside Kapila, the sage whose stillness was a brighter danger than any thief. The sons did not know that. They knew a rite had been insulted and their father was waiting.
line: They began to dig. A generation became a quarry.

title: They Dig the World
hook: The poem says they opened the earth until the noise reached the serpent-world below.
body: Oceans shifted to fill what they had removed. This is myth doing geology: a family's impatience written as landscape. They were not digging for water. They were digging for a slight.
line: At the bottom of the slight, a horse stood next to a quiet man.

title: They Find Kapila
hook: He was meditating. The horse was not his theft. The accusation was.
body: Sixty thousand voices decided a silent sage must be a robber because the evidence was nearby. Proximity is not guilt. They were too many to remember that.
line: Kapila opened his eyes. The rest of the sentence was light.

title: A Look That Burns
hook: His radiance, not a weapon he picked up, finished them.
body: They became ash where they stood, a field of sons reduced to the evidence of having been wrong in a holy place. The horse remained. Kapila returned to silence, which had been disturbed and was not apologetic.
line: Sagara's line now had a debt that water, not armies, would have to pay.

title: Amshuman Searches
hook: Asamanja's son went down into the dig, and he knew how to speak to a sage.
body: Kapila gave him the horse and the truth: these ashes will not rise for ordinary water. They need Ganga, who is in heaven, and who will not come because a grandson weeps politely.
line: Amshuman carried the horse home and the sentence home. The rite could end. The dead could not.

title: Bhagiratha
hook: Generations later a king in that line decided the sentence would not outlive him.
body: Bhagiratha set his body to tapas until Brahma had to answer. He did not ask for a palace. He asked for a river to be allowed to fall. The ash of sixty thousand was still a family matter.
line: Austerity, in his case, was an administrative act on behalf of the dead.

title: Brahma's Condition
hook: Yes, said Brahma, and then the condition that made the yes almost a no.
body: Ganga's fall will shatter the earth if nothing catches her. Ask Shiva. If he will hold her in his hair, the world can survive the kindness you are requesting.
line: Bhagiratha turned from one impossible assent to another. The river was willing to be proud. The mountain had to be willing to be humble.

title: Shiva Agrees
hook: The yogi who had burned desire agreed to catch a river, which is a stranger mercy.
body: He would take her on his head. He would not be swept. Bhagiratha's penance had worked twice: once on the god who could give the order, once on the god who could survive it.
line: The sky above the mountain thickened with water that had opinions.

title: She Falls
hook: Ganga came down intending to drown the god who had agreed to hold her.
body: Pride, even in a sacred river, is still pride. She threw her whole weight at his hair. Shiva did not step aside and did not boast. He let the coils take her, and she discovered that infinite water can be made into a secret.
line: The earth waited. For a while, nothing reached it.

title: Held
hook: Bhagiratha worshiped again, because a river trapped in hair is not yet a salvation.
body: Shiva, satisfied that Ganga had learned she was not the strongest thing in the sky, loosened a stream. One thread of her, humbled, was allowed to become a river on the ground.
line: The rest remained his. The poem likes this proportion: mercy released, pride still held.

title: He Leads Her
hook: Bhagiratha went ahead in his chariot, and the new river followed like a vow that had learned obedience.
body: Where he turned, she turned. Deserts became banks. People who had never seen this water came out of houses that would have to be rebuilt closer to it.
line: A king walking in front of a river is an image of dharma with a direction.

title: The Ashes Wake
hook: When her water touched the field of sons, the debt closed.
body: They rose, not as an army, as souls released from a mistake that had lasted longer than their bodies. Ganga earned the name Bhagirathi there, the river of the man who would not let his dead stay unfinished.
line: Rama, hearing the end of it beside the living water, understood why a road can be holy.

title: Gautama's Ashram
hook: They came to a courtyard where a woman sat and did not move.
body: Vishwamitra lowered his voice, which he did not do for demons. This is Ahalya, he said. The air around her was the air of a paused life. Rama did not step forward until the story was told.
line: The sage was teaching again: some rescues require you to know what you are touching.

title: How Indra Came
hook: The king of gods wanted her, and did not come as himself.
body: He wore Gautama's form, because deceit was the only door pride would fit through. Ahalya knew, in the harder telling, and in the gentler one she was deceived. The epic has carried both, and both leave Indra guilty.
line: Disguise is the theme. The cost will not be disguised.

title: The Curse
hook: Gautama returned and the air tore.
body: Indra was marked. Ahalya was sentenced to wait without a life, stone in the telling most people remember, dust and invisibility in the older verse, until the one who was coming walked this yard. The husband left. The wife remained as a paused sentence.
line: Rama heard the condition and understood it included him.

title: The Foot
hook: Vishwamitra told him to enter. The dust of his foot did what years had not.
body: Ahalya stood. Color, breath, tears: the ordinary glories of being a person returned in that order. She did not perform innocence. She performed gratitude, which is braver.
line: Gautama's curse had a door in it. Rama was the door.

title: She Is Returned
hook: The sage came back, and the marriage that had been a ruin agreed to be a house again.
body: No one in the yard pretended the past was clean. That is the mercy the scene offers instead: a person can be given back to herself without the story rewriting what happened.
line: Rama bowed, and they walked on toward a city that was making a bow into a marriage condition.

title: Mithila
hook: Janaka's city received them with the courtesy of a place that had hosted many kings and been impressed by few.
body: White houses, a court that liked philosophy, a daughter the streets already treated as a future they were not allowed to rush. Vishwamitra's name opened the gate faster than Rama's, because Rama's name was not yet a sound Mithila had needed.
line: It was about to.

title: Janaka Receives Them
hook: The king was a sage who had agreed to wear a crown, which made him rarer than his guests.
body: He honored Vishwamitra, fed the princes, and did not immediately produce the bow like a merchant. Rama watched a ruler who could sit inside a question without fidgeting. It was a kind of kinship.
line: In the morning Janaka would tell them why his daughter was still unwed.

title: The Plow
hook: I was turning the field for a sacrifice, Janaka said, and the earth turned up a child.
body: The furrow opened. A girl lay in it, not abandoned, offered. He lifted her and the lifting was the adoption. Sita, he named her, because sita is the furrow itself.
line: A daughter whose mother was the ground would one day call the ground mother again. The poem plants that rhyme here and does not underline it.

title: From the Earth
hook: She grew in Mithila as a princess who had not been negotiated into the family.
body: Janaka's wife raised her. The city claimed her. None of that canceled the first fact: she had come from soil, and soil does not forget its own. When she walked, people said the house seemed better arranged.
line: Her marriage would not be arranged by beauty alone. Her father had tied it to a feat.

title: The Vow
hook: Shiva's bow lay in the hall, and Janaka had sworn by it.
body: Whoever strings this will take Sita's hand. Not a test of wealth. A test the bow itself would grade. Kings had come for the daughter and gone home angry at an object.
line: Vishwamitra glanced at Rama. The glance was the permission the boy had not yet asked for.

title: Kings Who Failed
hook: They had been strong. The bow did not care.
body: Some could not shift it. Some shifted it and were finished. The hall kept a politeness over the humiliation, which made the humiliation worse. Sita watched from where a daughter watches her fate being mishandled by strangers.
line: Failure, repeated, starts to look like the nature of the thing. It was not.

title: He Asks to Try
hook: Rama did not stride. He requested.
body: May I, with the sage's leave and the king's. The courtesy mattered, because the act that followed would be told as pride if he had grabbed. Janaka said yes with the tired hope of a father who has hosted too many noes.
line: Rama walked to the bow as if the weight had already introduced itself.

title: The String
hook: He lifted it. The hall's breath became a single object.
body: The bow rose as if it had been waiting for this hand and was mildly offended by the others. He set the string. Wood and iron that had outlasted generations decided, at last, to be an instrument.
line: Sita, who had watched so many leave, did not look away.

title: The Sound
hook: The bow snapped. The crack was heard as thunder, and as permission.
body: People fell. Lamps shook. Janaka laughed the laugh of a man whose vow had finally agreed with his love. Vishwamitra did not look surprised. He looked finished with a task he had not announced in Ayodhya.
line: The garland, after that, was a small thing. It was also the marriage.

title: The Message
hook: Janaka sent riders south before the hall had finished ringing.
body: Come, he told Dasharatha. The bow is broken by your son, and my daughter is no longer a condition. She is a bride, if you will bring the house to meet her. The road filled with haste that felt like joy.
line: In Ayodhya an old king heard his boy's name attached to a miracle and did not sit down for a long time.

title: Dasharatha Comes
hook: He arrived with priests, brothers, and the relieved greed of a father who gets to attend the wedding instead of the funeral he had feared.
body: Bharata and Shatrughna were called from Kekaya. A marriage in this family is never allowed to be singular. Vashishtha walked in and the rites acquired their proper spine.
line: Rama bowed to his father in a city that had just watched him break a god's bow. The bow was the less difficult obedience.

title: Four Names
hook: Janaka's house did not marry off a daughter. It married a family.
body: Rama and Sita. Lakshmana and Urmila, Sita's sister. Bharata and Mandavi, Shatrughna and Shrutakirti, daughters of Janaka's brother Kushadhvaja. Four fires were planned because one would have been a lie about how these brothers lived.
line: The courtyard was measured for a joy that had to be wide.

title: Rama and Sita
hook: They took hands around a fire that had more witnesses than a kingdom usually allows.
body: She had come from earth. He had come from a bowl of payasam and a question Narada answered. None of that was spoken over the mantra. The mantra was enough. Their fingers met, and the epic's private life began in public.
line: Urmila watched her sister and learned the shape of her own hour, which was next.

title: The Other Three
hook: Lakshmana married Urmila, and the poem will owe her a quiet debt it only partly pays.
body: Mandavi took Bharata's hand. Shrutakirti took Shatrughna's. Four circles of flame, four garlands, one night in which Mithila and Ayodhya agreed about the future. The women were not prizes at the edge of the shot. They were the house the shot had entered.
line: Janaka gave them away and did not look poorer.

title: Gifts and Farewell
hook: Mithila tried to send a dowry large enough to embarrass a grateful man, and Dasharatha was appropriately embarrassed.
body: Elephants, gold, servants who would have to learn a new city's streets. Janaka's blessing was the lighter thing and the heavier. Go, he said, and be a house.
line: The chariots turned south. The bow's thunder was already a story the grooms were inside of.

title: A Fury on the Road
hook: The wedding weather broke. A man stood in the way with an axe and an older anger.
body: Parashurama, Rama in another age, the brahmin who had emptied the warrior class when it grew insolent. He had heard Shiva's bow break. He had not come to bless the procession.
line: The horses stopped. Joy discovered it had a border.

title: Whose Bow
hook: He spoke to Rama as if the others were audience.
body: You broke it. Shiva's bow. Do you know what you touched, or did a wedding make you careless. I have another bow, Vishnu's own. If you are only a boy who was lucky in a hall, this one will instruct you.
line: Dasharatha's mouth went dry. The father who had feared demons now feared a sage with a grievance against kings.

title: Vishnu's Bow
hook: Parashurama put it in Rama's hands and the procession became a test again.
body: It was heavier than the one that had broken, or it was heavier because of who offered it. Rama took it without the courtesy-theater of strain. Lakshmana's jaw set. The brahmin watched the fingers, not the face.
line: Stringing this would mean naming himself to someone who had the right to recognize him.

title: Where Shall It Land
hook: Rama strung it, set an arrow, and asked the question that ended the anger.
body: This cannot be drawn and not released. Where shall it fall. Your austerity, or the worlds that have not offended me. Choose. Parashurama heard his own name inside the politeness and understood the asker.
line: The axe, suddenly, was an old tool in the presence of its owner.

title: He Knows
hook: Parashurama yielded the merit of his tapas to the arrow's hunger and stepped off the road.
body: He was not defeated in the way armies are defeated. He was recognized, and recognition emptied him of the need to continue. He praised Rama, which from him was a surrender, and went toward the mountain he still had a right to.
line: The procession remembered how to breathe.

title: The Road Home
hook: South of that meeting, the wedding became a journey again.
body: Rama pointed nothing out. He did not need to. Sita was seeing the country that would later be taken from her, and the poem allows her this unharmed looking. Urmila rode toward a city she would inhabit more loyally than the men who left it.
line: Dasharatha counted the days backward from fear to arrival.

title: The Gates Open
hook: Ayodhya did not wait at the threshold. It came out.
body: Drums, women on the walls, a king entering with more children than he had left with and with daughters the city immediately began to love. Kausalya saw Sita and understood the bowl of payasam had been answered in a face.
line: The streets made a noise the poet compares, kindly, to an ocean that has decided to be happy.

title: Sita Enters the House
hook: The palace had to become large enough for four new women and the quiet between them.
body: Sita learned the corridors. Urmila learned which window faced the practice yard. The mothers-in-law were not a single weather. Kausalya's warmth, Kaikeyi's brilliance, Sumitra's steadiness: the house had climates, and the brides walked into all of them.
line: For now, every climate was kind. The book of childhood and marriage ends while that is still true.

title: The First Book Rests
hook: Valmiki sets the stylus down on a city that believes its joy has arrived to stay.
body: Rama is home. Sita is beside him. The bow is broken, the axe has gone up the mountain, the fathers are alive. Anyone ending here would call it a happy poem. The poet knows the leaf under this one.
line: Bala Kanda closes the way a held breath closes. The next breath is Ayodhya's, and it will hurt.

title: The Heir Is Named
hook: Ayodhya Kanda opens on a city preparing a joy it will not be allowed to finish.
body: Dasharatha is old. The ministers say what the streets have already decided: Rama should be yuvaraja. The king agrees with the relief of a man putting down a weight. Lamps are planned. The date is set. Sita hears it as a wife hears news that rearranges a house.
line: No one in the room is thinking of an old promise.

title: Manthara
hook: Kaikeyi's maid sees the lamps and understands them as a loss.
body: Manthara is not a demon in this poem. She is a servant who loves her queen's son more than the city's happiness, and she is very good at fear. She goes to Kaikeyi, who is pleased at Rama's rise, and stays until that pleasure is gone.
line: A kingdom can be turned by someone who is not in the council at all.

title: Two Boons
hook: Kaikeyi asks for the two gifts Dasharatha once placed in her hands, and she names them without blinking.
body: Bharata will be consecrated. Rama will go to the forest for fourteen years, in bark, as an ascetic, not as a prince on a hunt. The king, who has never refused her, finds that a promise kept can be a kind of death. He falls. He does not unsay it.
line: Valmiki does not soften the asking. The verse lets the room go quiet.

title: Rama Accepts
hook: They send for Rama as if the news were still a coronation.
body: He comes in the clothes of a man about to be crowned and hears a sentence of exile from his father's silence and his stepmother's mouth. He does not argue with the boon. He does not ask the king to break it. In Valmiki the obedience is immediate, and that immediacy is the whole character.
line: He goes to tell Sita, believing she will stay.

title: Sita Will Go
hook: Sita refuses the palace the way a person refuses a life that has already ended.
body: She will not be kept safe in Ayodhya while he walks. The poem gives her a long argument, and she wins it. Lakshmana does not ask. He has already chosen the road, and he leaves Urmila in the city. Later tellings will give Urmila a sleep that lasts the fourteen years. Valmiki gives her the harder thing: she stays awake, and she stays.
line: Three leave. A household learns what a door is for.

title: The Leaving
hook: The city comes into the road and will not let the chariot go cleanly.
body: Dasharatha follows until he cannot. Kausalya follows until the dust decides. Sumantra drives, and then, at the forest's edge, he is sent back with a message that is mostly a father's unbroken voice. Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana cross into the trees on foot. Behind them Ayodhya begins the work of becoming a city without its heir.
line: The king does not recover his stride. He will not recover his life.

title: Guha's Night
hook: At the river, the chieftain Guha meets them as a friend, not as a subject performing grief.
body: He offers his place, his food, his watch. Rama will not sleep in a bed. Lakshmana will not sleep at all: he stands the night with a bow while Guha keeps him company and learns what this exile is going to cost the people who love the prince. In the morning they cross. The boatman in later songs will ask to wash their feet. Valmiki's ferryman simply takes them over.
line: On the far bank, the city is already a rumor.

title: The King Dies
hook: Dasharatha dies calling a name the palace cannot answer.
body: Before the end he tells Kausalya the old guilt: as a young hunter he had loosed an arrow at a sound and killed a boy who was filling a pot for his blind parents, and the father cursed him to die of grief for a son. The curse arrives on time. Bharata is away in Kekaya. The throne sits in a house where no one will sit on it.
line: Ayodhya keeps the body and loses the meaning of morning.

title: Bharata Refuses
hook: Bharata comes home to a funeral and a crown, and he will take only one of them.
body: He has not asked for this. When he learns the boons were used in his name, his anger at his mother is the cleanest thing in the book. He will not be king over Rama's absence. He gathers the city, the mothers, the priests, and an army of grief, and he marches to the forest to bring his brother back.
line: The road south is full of people who agree with him and cannot change the vow.

title: The Sandals
hook: At Chitrakuta the brothers meet, and the forest does not give Bharata what he came for.
body: Rama will not return. Fourteen years were named, and a named promise is not a mood. Bharata asks, argues, weeps, and at last takes what can be carried back: Rama's sandals. He will set them above the throne at Nandigrama and rule as their servant, not as king. The city will be governed by a pair of wooden feet.
line: Ayodhya Kanda ends there. The exile has an heir, and the heir is an absence.

title: Panchavati
hook: Aranya Kanda settles them in a leaf-hut where five trees stand and a river keeps time.
body: Years have already been walked: sages sheltered, demons turned off the paths, the quiet labor of an exile that is also a protection. At Panchavati, Sita asks for a home that faces the water. Lakshmana builds it. For a while the poem is only weather, food, and the particular peace of three people who have learned each other's silences.
line: The peace is real. It is also the last of its kind.

title: Shurpanakha
hook: A rakshasi comes to the hut and wants Rama, and the afternoon turns.
body: Shurpanakha is Ravana's sister. Rama refuses her. The brothers mock the offer between them, and when she moves on Sita, Lakshmana cuts away her nose and ears. Valmiki records the mutilation without the later comfort that it was only a trick. She goes bleeding to her brothers. The forest, which had been a hermitage, remembers it is also a kingdom of rakshasas.
line: What follows is not a private insult. It is a war, arriving early.

title: Khara Falls
hook: Khara, Dushana, and fourteen thousand come for the hut, and Rama meets them alone.
body: He sends Sita and Lakshmana to a cave and stands in the open. The poem's battle here is terrible and exact: arrows, chariots, the names of the fallen. Khara dies. The news travels to Lanka by the one who fled it, Shurpanakha, and she tells it to Ravana in the only form that can move him. Your sister was maimed. A man in the forest did it. His wife is beautiful.
line: Ravana does not ride out in anger. He rides out in a plan.

title: The Golden Deer
hook: Maricha, who once was flung across the sea, comes back as a deer of gold.
body: Ravana has asked him to draw Rama out. Sita sees the animal and wants it. Rama knows the forest well enough to doubt, and he goes anyway, because she has asked, and because a husband in this poem is not only a warrior. He leaves Lakshmana with a charge: stay. Do not leave her, whatever voice you hear.
line: The deer, struck, dies in Maricha's own voice, crying for Lakshmana in Rama's tone.

title: The Line
hook: Later tellings draw a line in the dust and give it a law. Valmiki does not.
body: In the poem, Lakshmana hears the cry, refuses to believe it is Rama, and goes only when Sita, frightened and then angry, accuses him of wanting her in his brother's absence. The charge is unjust. He goes because of it. What the tradition calls the Lakshmana rekha is a later protection, a circle of obedience the poem itself does not draw. What the poem draws is worse: he leaves, and the door is only a door.
line: Ravana has been waiting for an empty threshold.

title: She Is Taken
hook: Ravana comes as a mendicant, and Sita steps forward with food.
body: He speaks, sheds the disguise, names himself, and takes her. She cries to the trees, the river, the animals, anyone who can carry a sentence. From the chariot she drops her ornaments toward the ground where someone might find a direction. The forest does not stop him. A vulture does.
line: The hut will be found empty. That emptiness is the rest of the epic.

title: Jatayu Falls
hook: Jatayu, old king of the vultures and a friend of Dasharatha, rises into the chariot's path.
body: He fights Ravana in the air with beak and talon and tears the chariot until he is broken for it. He cannot save her. He can do the other thing the poem requires: he can stay alive long enough to speak. When Rama and Lakshmana return to the ruined hut and follow the trail of flowers and gold, they find him dying, and he gives them the name. Ravana. South.
line: Rama holds him, and performs for a bird the rites of a father.

title: Shabari
hook: The road south passes a cursed body and ends, for a while, at a woman who has been waiting.
body: Kabandha, a rakshasa twisted out of his own shape, is freed by their swords and, dying back into himself, points them to Sugriva on the mountain. Before that alliance, they come to Shabari. She is an aged disciple whose teachers have gone on and left her the instruction to wait for Rama. The tasted berries are a later tenderness. Valmiki's gift is plainer and enough: she feeds them, she has kept the watch, and when they have gone she leaves her body like a task completed.
line: Aranya Kanda closes on a direction. Kishkindha is next, and it has a monkey for a door.

title: Hanuman
hook: On the shore of a lake, a minister in a monkey's body comes to learn who the two archers are.
body: Sugriva has been driven from Kishkindha by his brother Vali and trusts no one. He sends Hanuman. Hanuman approaches as a student of speech, sheds the disguise, and carries them to the exiled king. The ornaments Sita dropped are there. Sugriva weeps at them, then offers the only bargain the mountain has: help me kill the brother who took my wife and my kingdom, and my people will search the earth for yours.
line: They swear it at a fire. Rama has a friend, and the friend has a war of his own.

title: Vali Falls
hook: Vali is stronger than Sugriva, and Rama ends him from behind a tree.
body: The brothers fight. Sugriva is losing. Rama's arrow takes Vali in the chest. Dying, Vali asks the question the poem does not dodge: why, hidden, and for a quarrel that was not yours? Rama's answer is kingship, a brother's wrong, a promise already made. Readers have argued with that answer ever since. Vali accepts it enough to die in it, and gives his son Angada to the new order. Sugriva is king. Tara mourns. The search is sworn again.
line: It does not begin. The rains come down and shut the mountain.

title: The Rains
hook: Rama sits out the monsoon on a ridge and thinks of Sita in weather.
body: Sugriva, new to power, forgets the oath in wine and wives. Lakshmana goes down the mountain in a rage that almost becomes another killing, and the search is shaken awake. The vanaras go out in all directions. The southern party is the one that matters: Angada, Hanuman, Jambavan, and the rest, to the edge of the sea, where they despair, and where Sampati, Jatayu's brother, burned of his wings and listening, tells them the name of the island. Lanka. Across the water. And he tells them who can cross it.
line: Kishkindha Kanda ends with a shore and a task no one else can carry.

title: The Leap
hook: Sundara Kanda is Hanuman's book, and it begins with him remembering that he can.
body: A curse had folded his power away. The elders speak it back into him. He grows until the mountain feels him, then leaves the earth. The ocean puts obstacles in the air: a mountain that offers rest, a serpent-mother who wants to swallow, a demon who catches shadows. He answers each and does not stop. Lanka rises on the horizon like a city that believes the sea is a wall.
line: He comes down small again, on the far side, and the poem becomes a search through streets.

title: Ashoka
hook: He finds her at last under an ashoka tree, thin, guarded, and still herself.
body: Sita is not rescued in this book. She is seen. Ravana comes to the garden and asks again, and she refuses again, with a blade of grass between her and his wanting. She speaks of Rama as a fact the island has not managed to undo. Hanuman, hidden, watches a queen who has been a prisoner so long that hope arrives like a stranger she must test.
line: The garden is beautiful. That is part of the cruelty.

title: The Ring
hook: Hanuman speaks, and the proof between them is small enough to hide in a hand.
body: Rama's ring. Sita's jewel, the chudamani, to be carried back. He offers to take her away that night, on his back, across the same water. She refuses. Her reasons are the poem's: she will not be touched even by a rescuer's carrying, and Rama must come himself, because the wrong was public and the answer has to be. She sends him with a memory only a husband would know, so the message cannot be a trick.
line: A ring leaves the garden. A war is now a promise with evidence.

title: Lanka Burns
hook: He is caught on purpose, after he has let the city know a messenger came.
body: Ravana's court sees a monkey and does not see the danger. Vibhishana, the king's brother, says a messenger is not to be killed. They set Hanuman's tail on fire instead. He grows, and the burning becomes a tour of the roofs. Lanka takes the flame. He puts the fire out in the sea, returns to the ashoka tree to be sure Sita was not harmed by it, and then he is gone, north, over the water, toward a prince who has been waiting through a season.
line: Sundara Kanda ends with a sentence Rama can live on. I have seen her. She is alive. She waits.

title: Vibhishana Comes
hook: Yuddha Kanda begins with a brother who has already lost the argument at home.
body: Vibhishana tells Ravana to return Sita. Ravana banishes him. He crosses the sea alone and stands in front of Rama's camp, and the camp does not agree about him. Sugriva says a traitor is a traitor. Rama says a man who comes for refuge comes under dharma, and he takes him. Vibhishana is consecrated, there on the sand, as king of a city that has not yet fallen.
line: The war now has a map drawn by someone who knows the doors.

title: The Bridge
hook: The sea will not part for a plea until Rama has almost burned it, and then it asks for a bridge instead.
body: Nala, whose lineage knows how to make stone rest on water, directs the work. Monkeys and bears carry mountains. The later song in which a squirrel is stroked for helping is not in Valmiki. What is in Valmiki is labor: days of it, a causeway walking south, an army that has never left the continent learning the sound of an ocean under its feet. Lanka stops being a rumor.
line: They cross. The war is no longer a direction. It is a field.

title: Angada
hook: Before the killing, Rama sends Angada into the throne room with one more offer.
body: Return her, and live. Ravana refuses, and the refusal is proud rather than wise. Angada plants his foot and asks if anyone in that hall can move it, a challenge the court fails, and he leaves the way an envoy leaves when the answer has already chosen the battlefield. Rama looks at the city from across the lines and tells the soldiers, in grief, that this did not have to be.
line: Then the names of the dead begin.

title: The Serpent Noose
hook: Indrajit, Ravana's son, fights from inside a mist and binds the brothers in living snakes.
body: The nagapasha holds Rama and Lakshmana and a field of vanaras. The camp believes the war has closed. It has not. Garuda comes, the enemy of serpents and a being whose arrival is its own theology, and the coils loosen. They stand. The poem does not linger on the miracle. It returns them to the gate, because Lanka is still shut and the day is not over.
line: A father in the city hears that his greatest weapon has failed, and reaches for a larger one.

title: Kumbhakarna
hook: They wake the giant who sleeps for months, and he tells his brother the truth before he agrees to die for him.
body: Kumbhakarna says Sita should have been returned. He says it plainly, in the hall, and then he armors himself anyway, because he is that kind of brother. On the field he is a catastrophe with a mouth. The vanaras are gathered up and eaten and shaken off. Rama meets him at last with arrows that take him apart, and the poem records each fall of that huge body as if size were a form of grief.
line: Lanka learns the sound of a brother hitting the earth.

title: Indrajit Dies
hook: Before he can be killed, Indrajit shows them Sita, and kills what they are seeing.
body: It is an illusion, a woman made of magic in her likeness, cut down in front of the army so that Rama will break. He does break, for an hour. Vibhishana says the name of the trick. Then the real battle: Indrajit can only be ended at Nikumbhila, where he is midway through a rite that would have made him unkillable. Lakshmana goes. He breaks the rite, he fights the son who has been the city's sharpest weapon, and he kills him.
line: Ravana does not grieve like a king. He grieves like a father, and then he comes out himself.

title: The Mountain
hook: Ravana's spear, the shakti, takes Lakshmana, and the camp is suddenly a deathbed.
body: This is after Indrajit, not before. The brother who won the hard duel is the one who falls. The physician says there is an herb on a mountain in the north, and there is no time to be careful. Hanuman goes. He does not find the plant in the dark, so he brings the mountain. The scent wakes Lakshmana. The war, which had leaned toward an ending of the wrong kind, stands up again.
line: Rama looks at his brother the way he looked at him on the night they left Ayodhya.

title: Ravana Falls
hook: The last duel is a long day of weapons, chariots, and a man who will not put down a stolen life.
body: Ravana fights as what he is: learned, consecrated, enormous, and wrong. Rama cuts away heads and they return. The counsel comes to use the brahmastra, the arrow that was waiting for this and not for spectacle. It enters the chest. The king of Lanka falls, and the poem, which has hated his deed, still gives him the funeral of a great brahmin warrior. Vibhishana mourns the brother. Rama tells him to. There is no triumph in the instruction.
line: Sita is in the city, alive, and the next hour is harder than the arrow.

title: The Ordeal
hook: Rama speaks to Sita, in public, words that have burned every century since.
body: He says he fought for honor, not for her, and that she is free to go where she will. The poem records her answer as fire. She steps into a pyre. The god of fire returns her and says what the camp already knew and what a husband, in that hour, would not say he knew: she was not touched. Rama says he knew, and that the ordeal was for the people who would not have believed his knowing. Readers are not required to find this kind. The scene is in the book. It should be read as grief and as a fault, not as a lesson to repeat.
line: She comes out. The war is over. The marriage is not what it was.

title: The Coronation
hook: They go home in the flying chariot, and the fourteen years are exact.
body: Bharata has kept the sandals. He has kept the watch. He sees them and the kingdom becomes a kingdom again. Rama is consecrated with Sita beside him. Lakshmana, Bharata, Shatrughna, the mothers, Hanuman who will not quite belong to any one city: Ayodhya makes a noise it has been saving since the lamps of the first morning. The Yuddha Kanda could end on that sound, and for a long time people let it.
line: There is another book. It does not restore what the fire ordeal spent.

title: The Washerman
hook: Uttara Kanda begins years later, in a city that has a story it will not stop telling.
body: Rama is king and is trying to be the kind of king whose private life is public law. A washerman, sending his own wife away, says he is not Rama, to keep a woman who lived in another man's house. The sentence travels. It is unjust. It is also, in this book, enough. Rama does not shout the man down. He does the thing the book has been afraid of since Lanka: he decides that a king's wife can be asked to bear the people's doubt a second time.
line: Nothing in the telling asks you to admire the decision.

title: Sita Is Sent
hook: Lakshmana takes her to the forest and is forbidden to argue.
body: She is pregnant. She thinks they are going to the hermitages for a blessing. At the river he tells her. The poem gives him a collapse, and gives her a composure that is not forgiveness. She sends Rama no curse. She asks to be left with the sages, and Valmiki's ashram receives her. Lakshmana returns to a city and a brother he can barely look at. The sons who will sing this story are not yet born.
line: Urmila, Mandavi, Shrutakirti are still in the houses. The epic has always been carried by the women who remained.

title: Lava and Kusha
hook: In Valmiki's grove the twins learn the poem that is their own life, and they do not know it.
body: They sing the Ramayana before Rama at a sacrifice, the whole of it, in the meter that began with a bird. He hears his exile, his war, his fault, in the mouths of boys who have his face. The recognition is slow and then total. He asks for Sita. He asks, this time, for her to come before the people and speak her truth again, as if the fire had not been enough.
line: She comes. She has already decided what she will ask of the earth.

title: The Earth
hook: Sita asks the ground, which once gave her up into Janaka's field, to take her back if she has been true.
body: The earth opens. A goddess rises, a mother in the old sense, and receives her. It is not a punishment and not a trick. It is the only witness left that does not belong to the court. Rama reaches, and the furrow closes. The king who won Lanka stands in a silence the poem does not decorate. The boys remain. The song remains. She does not.
line: If the epic has a moral wound, it is this hour, and the poem keeps it open.

title: The Sarayu
hook: The poem ends in a river, and it does not pretend the ending is a repair.
body: Time, in the shape of an ascetic, comes to Rama and says the years of this life are done. Lakshmana hears a private counsel he was told not to interrupt, interrupts it to save a sage's dignity, and takes the consequence: he walks into the Sarayu first, and the water receives him as a return, not as a drowning. Then Rama. Then the brothers, the people who will not stay in a city without him, entering the river as a procession enters a temple.
line: Hanuman remains, asked to stay in the world as long as the story is told. Valmiki sets the stylus down. The krauncha that began it is quiet. The river is not.
